content:
[For folk literature,] you need folk allusions — if cowardly, say Vuu Dhahlang; if brave, say old Huang Dyung.
— Lǎo Shě, The Agony of Creating Popular Literature

I am the kind of person who emphasizes at the beginning of each smalltalk that I am a non-gamer. Unfortunately, this statement requires clarification. I open Tetris from time to time, and occasionally linger on neal.fun and Lichess, but Doom is beyond choice. I always make the claim abruptly, regardless of how others would interpret it, maybe contrary to my intention. I envy gamers, in fact. I envy them like the hypothetical narrator in a clichéd advertisement envies those who read. Their focus on games and the clear separation between games and work are beyond my imagination.
